Subject: Re: Redwood partnership intro — next steps

Kimberly / team,

Thanks again for the intro call today. Orion Workbench is excited about building a first-class connector to Redwood so our customers can pick Redwood as a managed inference option inside the Workbench deployment flow.

High-level asks from our side for the pilot:
- LangChain and LlamaIndex connector that maps Workbench document sources (S3 buckets / internal Postgres) to Redwood embeddings and runtime calls.
- Trace instrumentation that preserves request attribution through our SDK (so we can correlate workspace requests with Redwood traces).
- A short mutual action plan (M.A.P.) with milestones for sandbox, security review, and a production gating checklist.

Can you share a suggested kickoff agenda and a simple MAP template? We have internal security folks who will want to review SOC2/cirrus evidence.

Cheers,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Orion Workbench

1) Introductions & roles (10m)
2) Success criteria and scope walk-through (15m)

Can you do next Wednesday 10:00am PT for a 60-minute technical kickoff? If that works, we’ll share the MAP and an instrumentation snippet ahead of the call.

Thanks,

Hey Jason — quick answers inline and a small telemetry patch attached.

On 8/20/26 09:14, Jason Lee wrote:
> - Our S3 sources sometimes include large binary objects (images/videos). We plan to index metadata + OCR/text extracts; will Redwood’s embedding pipeline accept a mixed-length batch?

Yes — Redwood’s embedding ingestion accepts mixed-length inputs. Typical recommendation: chunk large text to ~1k token pieces for embedding, and attach a `source_chunk_id` so retrieval can reassemble. For images/video OCR transcripts, treat the transcript as text pieces; for heavy-duty media we recommend asynchronous batching using our batch-embed endpoint to avoid high tail latency.

> - For our internal audit, we need a list of Redwood endpoints that the connector will call and an expected token/embeddings QPS estimate for a 100-seat pilot.

Endpoints for connector MVP (subject to change):
- POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings (batch & stream variants)
- POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate (sync generation)
- POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/trace (ingest trace metadata)

QPS estimate for 100-seat pilot (very rough):
- Embeddings: 15–30 req/s (batching recommended)
- Generate: 5–15 req/s (depends on prompt fan-out)

Telemetry snippet (attached as patch): shows how to map Orion workspace_id to x-redwood-trace header. Please review; it’s intentionally tiny so you can paste into your SDK.

Jonas
Principal Engineer, Runtime Integrations
Redwood Inference
